title: Muffin-Tin Mini Frittatas with Spinach, Cheddar, and Red Pepper
description: Ten eggs, a pepper, and a handful of spinach make 12 small frittatas, about 50 cents apiece. Bake them on Sunday and they go into lunchboxes all week, cold or rewarmed.
notes: Silicone liners or a well-oiled metal tin release cleanly; paper liners stick to egg. The frittatas puff in the oven and sink as they cool, which is normal. For the lunchbox, pack them cold with an ice pack so they stay under 40°F until lunch. Refrigerate within 2 hours of baking and keep up to 4 days, or wrap individually and freeze up to 2 months, then thaw overnight in the refrigerator. To serve warm at home, microwave one for 30 to 45 seconds until it reaches 165°F in the center. For dairy-free frittatas, leave out the cheese and use unsweetened nut-free plant milk, which removes the milk allergen. Finely chopped broccoli or thawed frozen corn can stand in for the pepper; squeeze any frozen vegetable dry so the eggs do not weep.

ingredients.name: extra-virgin olive oil, divided, plus more for the tin
kosher salt, plus a pinch for the vegetables
shredded sharp cheddar cheese (4 oz, 113 g), divided

instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the center. Brush all 12 cups of a standard muffin tin generously with olive oil, or set silicone liners in the cups.

Warm 1 tablespoon of the oil in a 10-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the bell pepper and cook, stirring now and then, until soft, 4 to 5 minutes. Add the spinach and a pinch of salt and cook just until wilted, about 1 minute. Spread the vegetables on a plate to cool for 5 minutes so they do not start cooking the eggs.
In a 4-cup measuring cup or bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, salt, garlic powder, and a few grinds of pepper until no streaks of white remain.

Divide the cooked vegetables, scallions, and three-quarters of the cheese among the cups. Pour the egg mixture over, filling each cup about three-quarters full, then scatter the remaining cheese on top.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until the frittatas are puffed, the edges are lightly golden, and a knife slipped into the center of one comes out with no wet egg.
Let the frittatas cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then run a thin knife around each one and lift it out. Cool completely on a wire rack before refrigerating or packing.

title: Black Bean and Corn Quesadillas for the Lunchbox
description: A mashed bean filling holds the cheese in place, so these quesadillas stay together cold and do not turn greasy. One can of beans makes four, for under a dollar each.
notes: Cool the cooked quesadillas on a rack rather than stacked on a plate; trapped steam is what makes them soggy by lunchtime. Pack the wedges cold with an ice pack to keep them under 40°F, and send the salsa or sour cream in a separate small container. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days. To freeze, layer whole quesadillas with parchment in a freezer bag for up to 2 months; reheat in a dry skillet or a 350°F oven for about 10 minutes, until the center reaches 165°F. For gluten-free quesadillas, use 8 corn tortillas stacked in pairs, which removes the wheat. For dairy-free, replace the cheese with a second can of mashed beans and a little extra salsa, which removes the milk allergen.

ingredients.name: black beans (15 oz), drained and rinsed
tomato salsa or pico de gallo, drained of extra liquid
shredded monterey jack cheese (6 oz, 170 g)

instructions: In a medium bowl, mash half the black beans with the salsa, cumin, garlic powder, and salt until mostly smooth. Stir in the remaining whole beans and the corn.
Lay the tortillas flat. Spread a quarter of the bean mixture over half of each tortilla, leaving a 1/2-inch border, and top with a quarter of the cheese. Fold the bare half over and press gently.

Heat a 12-inch skillet over medium heat and brush it lightly with oil. Cook two quesadillas at a time until the bottoms are golden and crisp, 2 to 3 minutes. Flip and cook until the second side is golden and the cheese has melted, 2 to 3 minutes more. Repeat with the remaining oil and quesadillas.
Move the quesadillas to a wire rack and let them cool for 10 minutes, then cut each into 3 wedges with a sharp knife.
Let the wedges cool completely before packing them into lunch containers or refrigerating them.

title: Ditalini Pasta Salad with Chickpeas, Cucumber, and Mozzarella
description: Small pasta, chickpeas, and crunchy vegetables in a mild red wine vinegar dressing, sized for a child's fork. It tastes better on day two, at about $1.25 a portion.
notes: The pasta drinks up dressing as it sits, so stir in a spoonful of water or a splash of vinegar before packing if it looks dry. Keep it cold: pack it with an ice pack so it stays under 40°F until lunch. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days; do not freeze, because the cucumber and tomatoes turn watery. Elbow macaroni or small shells work in place of ditalini. Gluten-free pasta removes the wheat, and leaving out the mozzarella (or using diced avocado) makes it dairy-free. Skip pesto-based versions for nut-free schools, since most pesto contains pine nuts or other tree nuts.

ingredients.name: kosher salt, for the pasta water
low-moisture mozzarella, cut into small cubes (113 g)

instructions: Bring 4 quarts of water and 1 tablespoon kosher salt to a boil in a large pot. Add the ditalini and cook, stirring once or twice, until tender all the way through, about 1 minute past the package time for al dente.
Drain the pasta in a colander and rinse it under cold running water until it is cool to the touch. Shake off as much water as you can and let it drain for 2 minutes.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk the olive oil, red wine vinegar, mustard, oregano, garlic, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and a few grinds of pepper until the dressing looks creamy.
Add the pasta, chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes, and bell pepper and toss until everything is coated. Fold in the mozzarella and the basil, if using.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes so the pasta absorbs the dressing. Stir, taste, and add a pinch more salt if needed before dividing into lunch containers.

title: Freezer Bean, Rice, and Cheese Burritos
description: Two cans of pinto beans, a pot of rice, and a block of cheddar roll into 8 burritos for about $1 each. Wrap and freeze them, then heat one in the morning for a hot lunch.
notes: Let the filling and rice cool before rolling; hot filling steams the tortilla and makes it gummy after freezing. Frozen burritos keep 3 months, and refrigerated ones keep 4 days. To reheat, remove the foil, wrap the burrito in a damp paper towel, and microwave for 2 1/2 to 3 minutes, turning it over halfway, until the center reaches 165°F. For a hot lunch, wrap the heated burrito in foil and pack it in an insulated lunch bag; for a cold lunch, pack it with an ice pack so it stays under 40°F. For dairy-free burritos, leave out the cheese, which removes the milk allergen. Corn tortillas crack when rolled this full, so for gluten-free serve the filling as a rice bowl instead.

ingredients.name: long grain white rice (200 g), rinsed
pinto beans (15 oz each), drained, 1/2 cup of the liquid saved
shredded sharp cheddar cheese (8 oz, 227 g)

instructions: Combine the rinsed rice, water, and 1/2 teaspoon salt in a medium saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low, and cook for 18 minutes. Take the pan off the heat and let it stand, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and spread on a plate to cool.

While the rice cooks, heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring often, until soft and translucent, 6 to 7 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, and chili powder and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

Add the pinto beans, tomato sauce, saved bean liquid, and the remaining 3/4 teaspoon salt. Simmer for 5 minutes, then mash with a potato masher until mostly smooth and thick enough to hold its shape on a spoon. Spread the beans in the skillet off the heat and let them cool for 15 minutes.
Warm the tortillas, stacked and covered with a damp towel, in the microwave for 30 to 45 seconds so they fold without cracking.
Spread about 1/3 cup beans across the lower third of each tortilla, top with about 1/4 cup rice and 1/4 cup cheese, then fold in the sides and roll up tightly away from you.
Wrap each burrito in foil or parchment, place them in freezer bags, press out the air, and freeze flat. Refrigerate any you plan to eat within 4 days.

title: Soy-Ginger Chicken Onigiri-Style Rice Balls
description: Japanese-style rice balls with a small center of glazed chicken thigh. Half a pound of chicken fills 8 of them, about 60 cents each, and they pack neatly without a spoon.
notes: Shape the rice while it is still warm; cold rice will not stick together. Cooked rice must be cooled and refrigerated within 2 hours, so wrap the finished balls and chill them promptly, then pack them with an ice pack to stay under 40°F. Rice firms up in the refrigerator, so they are softest within 2 days; you can also wrap and freeze them for up to 1 month and microwave from frozen, still wrapped, for about 1 1/2 minutes until hot (165°F) in the center, then cool before packing. Pack the seaweed separately so it stays crisp and let your child wrap it at lunch; many seasoned seaweed snacks are made with sesame oil, so check the label if sesame is a concern. For gluten-free rice balls, use gluten-free tamari and a mirin labeled gluten-free, which removes the wheat. Leftover cooked chicken, chopped fine and tossed in the glaze, works in place of the thigh.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs (227 g), cut into 1/2-inch pieces

instructions: Rinse the rice in a bowl of cold water, swishing and draining 3 or 4 times until the water is nearly clear. Drain in a sieve for 15 minutes.

Combine the rice and water in a heavy medium pot and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting, and cook for 15 minutes. Take the pot off the heat and let it stand, covered, for 10 minutes.

While the rice cooks, heat the oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in a single layer and cook, stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through to 165°F, 5 to 6 minutes.

Add the ginger and stir for 30 seconds, then add the soy sauce, mirin, and sugar. Simmer, stirring, until the sauce coats the chicken and the pan is nearly dry, 1 to 2 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the scallion. Chop the chicken finely so it tucks into the rice, and let it cool.
Turn the rice into a wide bowl and let it cool for about 10 minutes, until you can handle it comfortably but it is still warm.

Set out a small bowl of water and the salt. Wet your hands, rub a pinch of salt over your palms, and scoop about 1/2 cup rice. Flatten it slightly, press a dent in the center, add a heaping tablespoon of chicken, and cover with a little more rice.

Press the rice firmly into a ball or triangle with 4 or 5 firm squeezes, turning as you go, until it holds together. Repeat with the remaining rice and chicken, wetting and salting your hands each time.
Wrap each rice ball tightly in plastic wrap and refrigerate. Pack a seaweed sheet alongside each one in a separate bag, if using.

title: Turkey and Veggie Cream Cheese Pinwheels
description: Flour tortillas spread with dill cream cheese and rolled around turkey, spinach, carrot, and cucumber, then sliced into spirals. No cooking, and four tortillas make 24 pieces.
notes: Spreading the cream cheese all the way to the far edge is what glues each roll shut, and chilling the rolls for an hour lets you cut clean spirals. Pat the cucumber and pepper strips dry so the tortillas do not get soggy. Pinwheels are a cold food: pack them with an ice pack so they stay under 40°F, and refrigerate within 2 hours. Whole wrapped rolls keep 3 days in the refrigerator and sliced pinwheels are best within 2 days; they do not freeze well. Deli meat should be heated until steaming (165°F) for anyone who is pregnant or has a weakened immune system, so for those eaters use leftover chicken cooked to 165°F and chilled. Sliced chicken from a batch of roasted thighs also costs less per pound than deli turkey. Hummus can replace the cream cheese for a dairy-free version; most hummus contains tahini, which adds sesame, and gluten-free tortillas remove the wheat.

ingredients.name: full-fat brick cream cheese, softened (170 g)
thinly sliced deli turkey breast (227 g)
english cucumber, cut into thin matchsticks and patted dry
red bell pepper, cut into thin strips

instructions: In a small bowl, stir the cream cheese, dill, garlic powder, and salt until smooth and easy to spread.
Lay the tortillas flat and spread each with about 3 tablespoons of the cream cheese in a thin, even layer all the way to the edges.
Cover each tortilla with a quarter of the turkey, leaving a 1-inch strip of bare cream cheese along the far edge. Lay a single layer of spinach over the turkey and scatter the shredded carrot on top.

Line up the cucumber and bell pepper strips in a row across the edge nearest you. Roll the tortilla up tightly away from you, tucking in the vegetables with the first turn, and press the seam against the bare cream cheese to seal.
Wrap each roll snugly in plastic wrap and refrigerate, seam side down, for at least 1 hour or up to overnight so the filling firms up.
Unwrap the rolls, trim off the ragged ends with a serrated knife, and cut each roll into 6 slices about 1 1/2 inches thick. Pack them snugly, cut side up, so they hold their shape.

title: Sesame-Free Chickpea Hummus Snack Boxes with Pita Chips
description: A mild, lemony hummus made without tahini, so it suits sesame-allergic kids, packed with crisp vegetables and oven-toasted pita chips. Two cans of chickpeas fill six boxes.
equipment: 6 lidded lunch containers with small dip cups
notes: Warming the chickpeas with their liquid softens the skins and gives a smoother hummus without peeling. This hummus has no tahini, but check the pita label, since some bakeries top their bread with sesame seeds or share equipment with them. Hummus is perishable: pack it with an ice pack so the box stays under 40°F until snack time, and refrigerate within 2 hours. The hummus keeps 5 days in the refrigerator or 1 month frozen (it turns slightly grainy, so stir well); cut vegetables keep 4 days in a container lined with a damp paper towel. Store the pita chips airtight at room temperature for up to 1 week and pack them in their own compartment so they stay crisp. For gluten-free boxes, swap the pita chips for corn tortilla chips, which removes the wheat.

ingredients.name: chickpeas (15 oz each), drained, 1/2 cup of the liquid saved
pita bread rounds, each cut into 8 wedges
carrots, peeled and cut into sticks
red bell pepper, cut into strips

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Toss the pita wedges on a rimmed baking sheet with 1 tablespoon of the olive oil and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt and spread them in a single layer.
Bake the pita for 8 to 10 minutes, turning the pan once, until golden and crisp at the edges. Let the chips cool completely on the pan; they crisp further as they cool.

Put the chickpeas and their saved liquid in a microwave-safe bowl and heat for 2 minutes, until hot. Meanwhile, process the garlic and lemon juice in a food processor for 30 seconds and let it stand while the chickpeas heat; this mellows the raw garlic.
Drain the chickpeas, keeping the liquid, and add them to the processor with the cumin and the remaining 3/4 teaspoon salt. Process for 1 minute, then scrape down the bowl.

With the motor running, pour in the remaining 3 tablespoons olive oil, then add the cold water and saved chickpea liquid a tablespoon at a time, processing for 2 to 3 minutes until the hummus is very smooth and creamy. Taste and adjust the salt and lemon.

Spoon about 1/3 cup hummus into each small dip cup and divide the carrots, cucumber, bell pepper, tomatoes (if using), and pita chips among the containers, keeping the chips in a dry compartment. Refrigerate until packing.

title: Broccoli Mac and Cheese Cups Baked in a Muffin Tin
description: Stovetop cheddar macaroni with chopped broccoli, set with one egg and baked into 12 sturdy cups. They hold their shape cold, so they pack like a muffin instead of a scoop.
notes: The 15-minute rest in the tin matters: the cups are soft when they come out of the oven and firm up as they cool. Elbow macaroni or small shells can replace the ditalini. Pack them cold with an ice pack to keep them under 40°F, or microwave one for 30 to 45 seconds to 165°F and send it in a thermos that you have preheated with boiling water for 5 minutes. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 4 days, or freeze in a single layer, then bag, for up to 2 months; thaw overnight in the refrigerator. For egg-free cups, leave out the egg; they will be softer but still hold in a lined tin, and the eggs allergen is removed. For gluten-free cups, use gluten-free pasta and thicken the sauce with 1 tablespoon cornstarch whisked into the cold milk instead of flour, which removes the wheat.

ingredients.name: kosher salt, for the pasta water
broccoli florets, fresh or frozen, chopped small (110 g)
unsalted butter (28 g), plus more for the tin
shredded sharp cheddar cheese (8 oz, 227 g), divided

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the center. Butter all 12 cups of a standard muffin tin generously, including the rims.
Bring 3 quarts of water and 1 tablespoon salt to a boil in a large pot. Cook the pasta for 2 minutes less than the package says, adding the broccoli for the last 2 minutes. Drain well in a colander.

In the same pot over medium heat, melt the butter. Whisk in the flour and cook, whisking, for 1 minute without letting it brown. Slowly whisk in the milk and simmer, whisking often, until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon, 3 to 4 minutes.

Take the pot off the heat and stir in the mustard powder, garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1 1/2 cups of the cheddar until melted and smooth. Let it cool for 2 minutes, then stir in the beaten egg.
Fold the pasta and broccoli into the sauce. Divide among the muffin cups, about 1/3 cup each, pressing down gently, and top with the remaining cheddar and the parmesan.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until the edges are golden and the cheese on top is bubbling.
Let the cups cool in the tin for 15 minutes so they set, then run a thin knife around each one and lift it out. Cool completely before refrigerating or packing.

title: Chewy Nut-Free Oat Bars with Sunflower Seeds and Raisins
description: School-safe granola bars made with toasted oats and seeds instead of nuts, held together with honey and butter. A pan of 16 costs about 25 cents a bar and keeps a week.
notes: Pressing the mixture hard into the pan and letting it cool completely are what keep the bars from crumbling. For nut-free classrooms, read the labels on the oats, seeds, and chocolate chips for shared-facility warnings about peanuts and tree nuts. The bars keep 1 week airtight at room temperature or 3 months frozen, and need no ice pack on their own. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year; pure maple syrup works in its place. Melted coconut oil can replace the butter for dairy-free bars, which removes the milk allergen if you also use dairy-free chocolate chips or leave them out. Dried cranberries can replace the raisins, and regular rolled oats are fine if you do not need the bars gluten-free.

ingredients.name: certified gluten-free old-fashioned rolled oats (225 g)

instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F. Line an 8x8-inch baking pan with parchment, leaving an overhang on two sides for lifting.

Spread the oats, sunflower seeds, and pumpkin seeds on a rimmed baking sheet and toast for 10 minutes, stirring once, until fragrant and lightly golden. Tip them into a large bowl and stir in the flaxseed, cinnamon, salt, and raisins.

In a small saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter with the honey and brown sugar. Bring to a simmer and cook, stirring, for 1 minute so the sugar dissolves completely. Take it off the heat and stir in the vanilla.
Pour the hot syrup over the oat mixture and stir until every oat is coated. If using chocolate chips, let the mixture cool for 5 minutes first, then stir them in so they do not melt completely.
Scrape the mixture into the lined pan and press it down very firmly with the bottom of a measuring cup, working into the corners, until compact and level.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the edges are golden brown. Cool completely in the pan on a rack, about 1 hour, then refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Lift the slab out by the parchment and cut it into 16 bars with a sharp knife. Wrap them individually or store them in an airtight container with parchment between the layers.

title: Thai-Inspired Pineapple Fried Rice with Egg, Peas, and Carrots
description: Day-old jasmine rice fried with scrambled egg, frozen peas and carrots, and seared pineapple, seasoned with soy and a mild curry powder. About $1.50 a serving, hot or cold.
notes: Use rice cooked at least a day ahead and refrigerated; freshly cooked rice clumps and turns gummy in the pan. Cooked rice is a food-safety risk if left out, so spread leftovers on a sheet pan, refrigerate within 1 hour, and keep up to 4 days, or freeze portions for up to 2 months. For a hot lunch, reheat a portion to 165°F and pack it in a thermos preheated with boiling water for 5 minutes; for a cold lunch, pack it with an ice pack so it stays under 40°F. Gluten-free tamari in place of the soy sauce makes it gluten-free and removes the wheat. Many restaurant versions add cashews; leave them out for nut-free schools. Leftover chicken thighs cooked to 165°F, diced, make it more filling, and drained canned pineapple tidbits work when fresh pineapple is expensive.

ingredients.name: cold cooked jasmine rice (640 g), preferably day-old
scallions, thinly sliced, whites and greens kept separate
frozen peas and diced carrots (200 g)
fresh pineapple, cut into 1/2-inch pieces (165 g)

instructions: Break up the cold rice with damp hands until the grains are separate. In a small bowl, stir together the soy sauce, curry powder, and sugar until the sugar dissolves.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Beat the eggs with the salt, pour them in, and stir gently until just set in large, soft curds, about 1 minute. Transfer to a plate.
Add another tablespoon of oil to the pan with the scallion whites and garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Add the peas and carrots and cook, stirring, until hot, about 2 minutes.
Push the vegetables to one side and add the pineapple to the open space. Let it sear without stirring until the edges brown, about 2 minutes, then stir it into the vegetables.

Add the remaining tablespoon of oil and the rice. Press the rice flat and let it sit for 1 minute to toast, then toss. Repeat for 4 to 5 minutes, until the rice is steaming hot and a few grains are crisp.

Pour the sauce over the rice and toss until evenly colored. Return the eggs, add the scallion greens and a few grinds of pepper, and toss to break the egg into bite-size pieces. Serve with lime wedges, if using, or cool quickly for packing.
